forum.title: STM32 Cube Programmer detects the nucleo but won't connect
forum.best_answer_content:
Here is your problem:

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/fd5fdf18-5ae2-46ee-b475-3eca87cb836e.png)

The Target microcontroller (the STM32H7) is not powered !

Check the board’s User Manual for how to correctly configure the power options.

**PS:**

> It used to work fine, but one day after we did some measurements it suddenly stopped

So did you change something to do those measurements ?

Or maybe you short-circuited something ?

Check power supplies.
forum.content_text:
Hi.

I’m working with a Nucleo H7A3ZI-Q. It used to work fine, but one day after we did some measurements it suddenly stopped refused to download code. I’m now trying to troubleshoot it.

When connected to STM32cubeprogrammer, the board is detected well, but it does not connect, and gives me this error:

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/6c9b04de-a315-4e21-b584-32816840126c.png)

and this error in the fail.txt: The interface firmware FAILED to reset/halt the target MCU

I am also able to update the card with STLink Updater through STLink-V3, which I have done succesfully, but the result remains the same. I have tried on a mac and a windows.
forum.author: CopperMoon

scraped_replies.html:
Here is your problem:

 

The Target microcontroller (the STM32H7) is not powered !

Check the board’s User Manual for how to correctly configure the power options.

 

PS:

It used to work fine, but one day after we did some measurements it suddenly stopped

So did you change something to do those measurements ?

Or maybe you short-circuited something ?

Check power supplies.
scraped_replies.author: Andrew Neil

scraped_replies.html:
I only changed the program, however a short circuit is very possible. I’ll check if the card works with a different power source, thank you! I have been using the USB-A to micro-b cable but maybe the port or the cable itself is damaged or the board requires more than 500mA for whatever reason. 

(To be clear, I did not add extra wiring to the board, but someone else has been using it, so it is possible that human error caused the issue.)
scraped_replies.author: CopperMoon

scraped_replies.html:
I only changed the program, .)

So what, exactly, did you change ?

In particular, have you introduced low power modes and/or reconfigure or disabled the SWD pins?
